investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit=100) on POST /api/agents
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict on POST /api/agents because the swarm backend reports the agent quota has been exceeded (limit is 100). The eval environment cannot provision a new agent, so no vmId or remoteState evidence is produced, causing all assertions in the expected-output contract to go unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100. At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T17:13:59Z–17:14:02Z), the quota was already at or above the limit, so every POST /api/agents call in the production environment was rejected with a 409 "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" error before any VM could be provisioned. This is not a code defect in the agent-creation path itself; it is a resource-limit enforcement by the swarm layer. The root cause is that the production swarm account/namespace used by the AURA eval harness has reached its maximum concurrent agent count of 100, leaving no capacity for the eval to create a new agent.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (latency 1241ms, ended 17:14:00), remote-agent-state (latency 1059ms, ended 17:14:01), remote-agent-runtime (latency 1014ms, ended 17:14:02).

Error body is identical across all three checks: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states: 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming a hard capacity ceiling rather than a transient network or auth failure.
All three checks produced empty evidence objects {}, meaning no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured — consistent with the request being rejected before any provisioning occurred.

Latency for all three failing calls is well under the warning threshold (30000ms) and outage threshold (120000ms), confirming the 409 is returned immediately by the quota-enforcement layer, not a timeout.
The check is marked required:true and staleAfterMinutes:20, meaning this failure will persist and escalate until quota is freed or raised.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The production swarm namespace/account used by the AURA eval harness has accumulated 100 live agents (from prior eval runs, leaked agents, or production workloads sharing the same quota pool) and none have been cleaned up, leaving zero capacity for new provisioning.
[Likely] Prior eval runs failed to delete their provisioned agents (e.g., due to a teardown bug or interrupted run), causing agents to accumulate over time until the quota ceiling was hit.
[Possible] The eval harness and production user workloads share the same swarm quota pool, and organic user growth in concurrent agents has consumed the remaining capacity.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a swarm configuration change, causing previously-acceptable usage to now exceed the new ceiling.
[Less likely] A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting active agents and reporting the quota as exceeded even if actual live agent count is below 100.

reproductionSteps.details: Expect an immediate HTTP 409 response with error code 'conflict' and message 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' if the quota is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.details: Filter the agent list for agents created by the AURA eval harness (e.g., by name prefix, label, or tag) and check their age and state. Agents older than the staleAfterMinutes threshold (20 min) that are still alive are candidates for leaked resources.

reproductionSteps.details: Delete one or more stale agents via the swarm API, then immediately retry POST /api/agents to confirm the quota error resolves and a new agent can be provisioned.

reproductionSteps.label: Check swarm quota configuration for the production namespace
reproductionSteps.details: Retrieve the quota settings for the swarm account/namespace to confirm the current limit is 100 and whether it has been recently changed.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Checks Failing with 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval harness cannot provision a new agent, so no agent ID, ready state, or runtime state can be collected, causing every downstream check in the remote-agents feature to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard agent quota of 100. At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T17:14:00–02Z), that quota was already at or above its limit for the target org or environment, so POST /api/agents returned 409 "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" for every creation attempt. Because the eval harness depends on successfully creating a fresh agent before it can poll state or verify runtime readiness, all three checks fail at the creation step with identical error payloads. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence in the supplied data indicates production user traffic is impacted.
proof: remote-agent-create check: POST /api/agents → HTTP 409, error: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", endedAt 2026-06-14T17:14:00.784Z
remote-agent-state check: POST /api/agents → HTTP 409, identical error payload, endedAt 2026-06-14T17:14:01.843Z, latencyMs 1059
remote-agent-runtime check: POST /api/agents → HTTP 409, identical error payload, endedAt 2026-06-14T17:14:02.857Z, latencyMs 1014
All three sibling checks share the exact same error message and code ("conflict"), confirming a single upstream rejection point at POST /api/agents rather than three independent failures

Expected output contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, and state — none of these fields are present in any check's evidence object, consistent with failure at agent creation before any state can be observed
Latency for all three calls is well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (5000ms), ruling out a timeout or performance degradation as the cause
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval environment's org or account has accumulated 100 live swarm agents (the hard quota limit) from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new agent creation.
[Likely] A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before its teardown/cleanup step, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Possible] The quota limit of 100 is shared across multiple concurrent eval pipelines or environments (e.g., staging and production share the same swarm org), and parallel runs exhausted the limit.
[Less likely] The quota ceiling was recently lowered by a configuration change on the swarm backend, causing previously-passing runs to now breach the limit.
[Less likely] The eval harness is not scoped to a dedicated eval org/account and is competing with real provisioned agents for quota headroom.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Agent Quota Exceeded (409 Conflict) Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T17:14Z with identical 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval harness cannot provision a new agent to run its lifecycle test, so no expected-output contract evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the "hello from aura" assertion was never reached.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm environment has hit its hard agent quota limit of 100 agents. Every POST /api/agents call from the eval harness is rejected with HTTP 409 and the nested error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because agent creation is the first step in the eval lifecycle, all downstream checks (state, runtime) fail before any agent is provisioned, producing a cascade of identical 409 failures across all three sibling checks. This is an eval-blocking infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect in the agent runtime itself; there is no evidence of a user-traffic or production-service outage beyond the eval's inability to create a new agent.
proof: remote-agent-create check: POST /api/agents → HTTP 409, error: 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', endedAt 2026-06-14T17:14:00.784Z
remote-agent-state check: POST /api/agents → HTTP 409, identical error body, endedAt 2026-06-14T17:14:01.843Z
remote-agent-runtime check: POST /api/agents → HTTP 409, identical error body, endedAt 2026-06-14T17:14:02.857Z, latencyMs 1014
All three checks share the same outer error code 'conflict' and nested swarm error 'conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100'
No evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were populated in any check — confirming agent creation never succeeded
The 'hello from aura' message assertion was never evaluated because the runtime step was never reached
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval harness creates a new agent on each run but does not reliably clean up (delete) previously created eval agents, causing quota to accumulate over repeated runs until the 100-agent hard limit is reached.
[Likely] A prior eval run, deployment, or manual test left orphaned agents in the swarm that were never deleted, consuming quota slots that are now unavailable to new eval runs.

[Possible] The swarm-level quota of 100 agents is shared between eval/test agents and real user-provisioned agents; growth in real user agents may have consumed quota that the eval previously relied on.
[Less likely] The quota limit itself (100) is misconfigured or too low for the current scale of the production environment, causing legitimate capacity exhaustion rather than a cleanup failure.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately after session open because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. The required evidence fields `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` were never populated, causing the eval to fail its output contract assertions.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The stream received a 404 response when attempting to open a session, which terminated the stream at the `generation_error` frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED. No generation progress frames or completion artifact signals were ever emitted. This is an eval-environment infrastructure failure localized to the agent runtime harness endpoint; there is no evidence of impact to production user traffic from this eval alone.
proof: The `generation_error` frame carries code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream sequence contains only three frames: generation_start → generation_error → empty message. No generation_progress or generation_completed frames were emitted.
Required evidence fields `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` are explicitly listed as missing in the check message.
The eval completed in 2021 ms — well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms — confirming the failure was an immediate hard error, not a latency or timeout issue.
The check ran in the `production` environment, meaning the harness endpoint configured for that environment returned 404 at 2026-06-14T17:14:02.857Z.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The agent runtime harness is not deployed or not running at the URL configured in LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL for the production eval environment, causing every session-open request to 404.

[Likely] The harness was deployed but the route or path for the session-open endpoint changed in a recent version, making the configured URL stale (version incompatibility as noted in the error message).
[Possible] The harness is running but behind a proxy or load balancer that is misconfigured, dropping requests to the specific session-open route with a 404 before they reach the harness process.

[Less likely] An environment variable (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL) was not injected into the eval runner for the production environment, causing the harness URL to resolve to a default or empty value that returns 404.

reproductionSteps.label: Confirm the harness URL configured for the production eval environment
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL and SWARM_BASE_URL environment variables in the eval runner's production configuration to verify they point to an expected, reachable host and path.

reproductionSteps.label: Probe the harness session-open endpoint directly
reproductionSteps.command: curl -v "$SWARM_BASE_URL" (or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL) and check for a 404 response
reproductionSteps.details: Issue an HTTP request to the configured base URL to confirm whether the harness process is reachable and whether the endpoint path is correct.

reproductionSteps.label: Check harness deployment status in the production eval environment
reproductionSteps.details: Verify that the agent runtime harness service or container is running and healthy in the environment where the eval executes. Look for recent restarts, failed deployments, or missing replicas.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the image-generation-stream eval after confirming harness reachability
reproductionSteps.details: Once the harness is confirmed reachable, re-trigger the eval to verify that generation_start → generation_progress → generation_completed frames are emitted and imageUrlPresent resolves to true.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed immediately after session open because the agent runtime returned a 404, emitting a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame before any progress or completion frames could be produced. The required evidence fields `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` were never populated, causing the eval to fail its output contract assertions.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness is unreachable at the configured endpoint (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). The stream received a 404 response when attempting to open a session, which terminated the stream at the `generation_error` frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED. No generation progress frames or completion artifact signals were ever emitted. This is an eval-environment infrastructure failure localized to the agent runtime harness endpoint; there is no evidence of impact to production user traffic from this eval alone.
proof: The `generation_error` frame carries code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message: 'agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version.'
The stream sequence contains only three frames: generation_start → generation_error → empty message. No generation_progress or generation_completed frames were emitted.
Required evidence fields `frameTypes` and `imageUrlPresent` are explicitly listed as missing in the check message.
The eval completed in 2021 ms — well under the warning threshold of 180000 ms — confirming the failure was an immediate hard error, not a latency or timeout issue.
The check ran in the `production` environment, meaning the harness endpoint configured for that environment returned 404 at 2026-06-14T17:14:02.857Z.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The agent runtime harness is not deployed or not running at the URL configured in LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL for the production eval environment, causing every session-open request to 404.

[Likely] The harness was deployed but the route or path for the session-open endpoint changed in a recent version, making the configured URL stale (version incompatibility as noted in the error message).
[Possible] The harness is running but behind a proxy or load balancer that is misconfigured, dropping requests to the specific session-open route with a 404 before they reach the harness process.

[Less likely] An environment variable (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL) was not injected into the eval runner for the production environment, causing the harness URL to resolve to a default or empty value that returns 404.

reproductionSteps.label: Confirm the harness URL configured for the production eval environment
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL and SWARM_BASE_URL environment variables in the eval runner's production configuration to verify they point to an expected, reachable host and path.

reproductionSteps.label: Probe the harness session-open endpoint directly
reproductionSteps.command: curl -v "$SWARM_BASE_URL" (or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL) and check for a 404 response
reproductionSteps.details: Issue an HTTP request to the configured base URL to confirm whether the harness process is reachable and whether the endpoint path is correct.

reproductionSteps.label: Check harness deployment status in the production eval environment
reproductionSteps.details: Verify that the agent runtime harness service or container is running and healthy in the environment where the eval executes. Look for recent restarts, failed deployments, or missing replicas.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the image-generation-stream eval after confirming harness reachability
reproductionSteps.details: Once the harness is confirmed reachable, re-trigger the eval to verify that generation_start → generation_progress → generation_completed frames are emitted and imageUrlPresent resolves to true.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded (limit=100) on POST /api/agents
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing with HTTP 409 Conflict on POST /api/agents because the swarm backend reports the agent quota has been exceeded (limit is 100). The eval environment cannot provision a new agent, so no vmId or remoteState evidence is produced, causing all assertions in the expected-output contract to go unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100. At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T17:13:59Z–17:14:02Z), the quota was already at or above the limit, so every POST /api/agents call in the production environment was rejected with a 409 "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" error before any VM could be provisioned. This is not a code defect in the agent-creation path itself; it is a resource-limit enforcement by the swarm layer. The root cause is that the production swarm account/namespace used by the AURA eval harness has reached its maximum concurrent agent count of 100, leaving no capacity for the eval to create a new agent.
proof: POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 on all three sibling checks: remote-agent-create (latency 1241ms, ended 17:14:00), remote-agent-state (latency 1059ms, ended 17:14:01), remote-agent-runtime (latency 1014ms, ended 17:14:02).

Error body is identical across all three checks: {"error":"swarm agent already exists: {\"error\":{\"code\":\"conflict\",\"message\":\"conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100\"}}","code":"conflict","details":null}
The inner swarm error explicitly states: 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100', confirming a hard capacity ceiling rather than a transient network or auth failure.
All three checks produced empty evidence objects {}, meaning no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was captured — consistent with the request being rejected before any provisioning occurred.

Latency for all three failing calls is well under the warning threshold (30000ms) and outage threshold (120000ms), confirming the 409 is returned immediately by the quota-enforcement layer, not a timeout.
The check is marked required:true and staleAfterMinutes:20, meaning this failure will persist and escalate until quota is freed or raised.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The production swarm namespace/account used by the AURA eval harness has accumulated 100 live agents (from prior eval runs, leaked agents, or production workloads sharing the same quota pool) and none have been cleaned up, leaving zero capacity for new provisioning.
[Likely] Prior eval runs failed to delete their provisioned agents (e.g., due to a teardown bug or interrupted run), causing agents to accumulate over time until the quota ceiling was hit.
[Possible] The eval harness and production user workloads share the same swarm quota pool, and organic user growth in concurrent agents has consumed the remaining capacity.
[Less likely] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered by a swarm configuration change, causing previously-acceptable usage to now exceed the new ceiling.
[Less likely] A swarm-side bug is incorrectly counting active agents and reporting the quota as exceeded even if actual live agent count is below 100.

reproductionSteps.label: Attempt to create a new remote agent via the API in the production environment
reproductionSteps.details: Expect an immediate HTTP 409 response with error code 'conflict' and message 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100' if the quota is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Query the current live agent count in the swarm namespace used by the eval harness
reproductionSteps.details: Use the swarm admin API or dashboard to list all agents in the production namespace/account and count how many are in a non-terminal state (running, idle, ready, pending). Confirm whether the count is at or near 100.

reproductionSteps.label: Identify agents that are stale or leaked from previous eval runs
reproductionSteps.details: Filter the agent list for agents created by the AURA eval harness (e.g., by name prefix, label, or tag) and check their age and state. Agents older than the staleAfterMinutes threshold (20 min) that are still alive are candidates for leaked resources.

reproductionSteps.label: Attempt agent deletion for a known stale eval agent, then retry POST /api/agents
reproductionSteps.details: Delete one or more stale agents via the swarm API, then immediately retry POST /api/agents to confirm the quota error resolves and a new agent can be provisioned.

reproductionSteps.label: Check swarm quota configuration for the production namespace
reproductionSteps.details: Retrieve the quota settings for the swarm account/namespace to confirm the current limit is 100 and whether it has been recently changed.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Checks Failing with 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) are failing simultaneously with HTTP 409 Conflict because the swarm backend is rejecting new agent creation with "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval harness cannot provision a new agent, so no agent ID, ready state, or runtime state can be collected, causing every downstream check in the remote-agents feature to fail.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard agent quota of 100. At the time of the eval run (2026-06-14T17:14:00–02Z), that quota was already at or above its limit for the target org or environment, so POST /api/agents returned 409 "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" for every creation attempt. Because the eval harness depends on successfully creating a fresh agent before it can poll state or verify runtime readiness, all three checks fail at the creation step with identical error payloads. This is an eval-environment resource exhaustion issue; no evidence in the supplied data indicates production user traffic is impacted.
proof: remote-agent-create check: POST /api/agents → HTTP 409, error: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", endedAt 2026-06-14T17:14:00.784Z
remote-agent-state check: POST /api/agents → HTTP 409, identical error payload, endedAt 2026-06-14T17:14:01.843Z, latencyMs 1059
remote-agent-runtime check: POST /api/agents → HTTP 409, identical error payload, endedAt 2026-06-14T17:14:02.857Z, latencyMs 1014
All three sibling checks share the exact same error message and code ("conflict"), confirming a single upstream rejection point at POST /api/agents rather than three independent failures

Expected output contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, and state — none of these fields are present in any check's evidence object, consistent with failure at agent creation before any state can be observed
Latency for all three calls is well under the warningLatencyMs threshold (5000ms), ruling out a timeout or performance degradation as the cause
possibleCauses: [Most likely] The eval environment's org or account has accumulated 100 live swarm agents (the hard quota limit) from previous eval runs that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new agent creation.
[Likely] A prior eval run crashed or was interrupted before its teardown/cleanup step, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
[Possible] The quota limit of 100 is shared across multiple concurrent eval pipelines or environments (e.g., staging and production share the same swarm org), and parallel runs exhausted the limit.
[Less likely] The quota ceiling was recently lowered by a configuration change on the swarm backend, causing previously-passing runs to now breach the limit.
[Less likely] The eval harness is not scoped to a dedicated eval org/account and is competing with real provisioned agents for quota headroom.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed simultaneously at 2026-06-14T17:14Z with identical 409 Conflict responses indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached. The eval harness cannot provision a new agent to run its lifecycle test, so no expected-output contract evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the "hello from aura" assertion was never reached.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm environment has hit its hard agent quota limit of 100 agents. Because agent creation is the first step in the eval lifecycle, all downstream checks (state, runtime) fail before any agent is provisioned, producing a cascade of identical 409 failures across all three sibling checks. This is an eval-blocking infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect in the agent runtime itself; there is no evidence of a user-traffic or production-service outage beyond the eval's inability to create a new agent.
